column1: # Expected is matched as a PREFIX of the outcome, so "MISS" matches "MISS(<base>)".
# Outcomes: HIT | MISS(<tokens>) | WRONG(config folder) | WRONG(unrelated folder) | SKIP
# Every line here was a MISS or a WRONG before <base>/<root>/<storeUserId> and tag filtering
# landed. They are kept as HIT so the gain cannot silently regress.
# --- were MISS: needed tokens PathResolver did not implement ---

column1: # --- malformed manifest entries: refusing them is the CORRECT answer ---
# Both lack a usable placeholder, so they designate a path anchored outside every root we know.
# SKIP rather than MISS because the fixture builder will not create them either — there is nowhere
# inside the scratch tree they could go. Returning nothing makes the user pick a folder; returning
# "/AppData/..." or "E:\AppData\..." would look authoritative and be wrong.
